get.description: Poll this while an import is running. An upload's progress is `imported_messages` / `total_messages`; its total grows a part at a time, as each export part is opened. A bot import's total grows with every page it reads from Discord, so its progress is `channels_done` / `channels_total`: the channel and thread rows being imported, and how many of those are finished (imported, or skipped because Discord no longer showed them to the bot). Both are null for an upload, and for a bot import that is not queued, running, completed, failed or cancelled. While an import is being deleted (`purging`), `purged_messages` counts the messages deleted so far, out of `imported_messages`; the count can stop short of that total, so `purged` is what says the deletion finished.
get.summary: Import detail and progress

delete.description: Removes the imported messages, their attachments, the channels the import created once they hold nothing else, and the uploaded archive objects. The roles it created stay, and the job row survives as the record that it happened.

get.description: What the Watch view polls while a bot import runs (#2857): the channel and thread rows by status and per Discord category, the ones running now, the last ones finished, and the failures with their reasons, each with the Frapp channel it lands in once known. A few KB whatever the server holds; `GET :id/channels` is the full list, which is too large to poll. The rows follow a bot import's walk, one channel at a time in `position` order; an upload works through export parts, which leave its rows' order and a skipped part's row unrecorded, so the web shows this for bot imports only.

put.description: Each Discord role becomes an existing Frapp role, a new role, or nothing (#2818). The mapping decides who reads the channels imported "Same as Discord"; starting the import creates the new roles and grants each role the read permission of the channels gated on it. It never assigns anyone to a role. Mapping anything other than `ignore` also needs `roles:manage`, since it creates roles and grants permissions.

post.description: Lists every channel in the server, and the threads of each channel the bot can read, and records them against this import, all set to `skip` until mapped. Each channel carries whether the bot can read it and whether it was private in Discord. Also returns the guild’s roles for the role step (every role but `@everyone` and the managed bot and booster roles) and, on each private channel, which of them could read it; and any warnings about what could not be read.

put.description: Send a decision for each top-level channel the scan found. Threads are not addressable — each one follows its parent’s decision, because the admin was asked about the parent and a thread is part of that conversation. A channel the scan did not return is rejected rather than added. A channel the bot cannot read can only be skipped, and a new channel needs `new_channel_visibility` unless the scan saw it was public in Discord and holding no private thread.

properties.description: Behavioral, content-free properties. Values must be scalars (string/number/boolean/null); keys that look like content/PII (content, body, email, name, …) are rejected, and so are `app` and `$`-prefixed keys, which the API sets itself.

accept_terms_privacy.description: The admin accepted the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, for the chapter and for themselves. Must be true (spec/behavior/legal.md). The acceptance timestamp and policy version are recorded server-side from the session — never from this payload.

from_chapter_level.description: True when the level comes from the member's chapter-wide chat level (GET /v1/channels/notification-preferences/chapter), not from this channel's own setting or default, so a client can label it "your default".

kind.description: A `chat_messages.kind`. `imported` and `loading` are absent by design — the first is refused by the push worker before any preference is read, and the second is an internal optimistic placeholder rather than a category of message a member receives.

level.description: The member's chapter-wide override for this kind, or null when they have set none. For the effective level of a real message, read GET /v1/channels/notification-preferences.

all = each channel at its own default; mentions = "Mentions and DMs only": every ordinary channel acts as mentions, while DMs, group DMs and the announcements channel keep notifying. A level the member set on one channel, or on a message kind, still wins.

is_read_only.description: Replaced by `who_can_see` and `who_can_post` (#3722); kept so an open page from before the change gets a clear refusal. A value that would change who can see or post is refused with a reload message.

default_notification_level.description: The channel's default push level for members who have set none of their own (#2771). Null clears it back to the built-in default: `all` for #general and the announcements channel, `off` for #chapter-audit, `mentions` for the rest. A member's own channel or kind level always wins. Refused on a DM or group DM, which always default to `all`.

is_default.description: Make this the chapter's default channel, where Chat opens for a member whose device has no last channel (ahead of #general). Setting it moves the default off any other channel; `false` on the current default leaves the chapter with none. Refused as `true` on a DM or group DM.

activity_excluded.description: Leave out of Activity (#3897): sign-up links posted here never reach anyone's Activity page, for channels like #advertising whose links aren't chapter business. Refused as `true` on a DM or group DM.

display_locked.description: True sets the channel to Always formal for every member; false lets each member pick their own display there again.

role_rank.description: The `display_order` of the member's highest role (lower ranks higher), or null when they hold no role. For sorting the list; names, avatars and role colors come from `GET /v1/members/roster`.

role_id.description: The id of that highest role, which the list groups readers under, or null when they hold no role.

role_name.description: That role's name, the group's heading, or null when they hold no role.

user_id.description: The `users.id` to add. Must be a member of the channel's chapter.

who_can_see.description: Who can see the channels that match this category (#3722): null for everyone in the chapter, or `tier:<id>` / `role:<id>` entries. A new channel in the category starts with it.

who_can_post.description: Who can post in the channels that match this category: null for everyone who can see them, or `tier:<id>` / `role:<id>` entries.

who_can_see.description: Who can see the channels that match this category (#3722): null for everyone in the chapter, or `tier:<id>` / `role:<id>` entries. Changing it changes every channel in the category that matched it, and only those.

who_can_post.description: Who can post in the channels that match this category: null for everyone who can see them, or `tier:<id>` / `role:<id>` entries.

content.description: The reply’s text, cut to 500 characters.

attachment_count.description: The reply’s `metadata.attachment_count`, or 0 when it has none.

sender_blocked.description: Set by a read that masks: true when the viewer blocked this replier, with `content` withheld (empty) and `kind` null; false when cleared. Absent on the Realtime echo, which carries the preview raw: a client applies its own list.

sender_id.description: Null for an imported archive message, which names its author in author_name instead. Kept on a masked row: the blocker chose the block, so reading their own list back is not a disclosure — and without it a client cannot reconcile a server-masked row against the list it applies itself.

content.description: Reads the masking sentinel when `sender_blocked` is true, and “[message deleted]” once the message is deleted. **Never pattern-match either string** — the machine-readable signals are `sender_blocked` and `is_deleted`.

kind.description: Null on rows written before the column existed; read as 'text'.

payload.description: Inline card payload for rich kinds. Null on a masked row — a points / task / event card is authored by the acting member and interpolates their free text — and on a deleted one, whose card data the delete removed (#1575).

metadata.description: Free-form annotations; carries `attachment_count`, and `attachment_photos` (one `{width, height, thumbhash}` per photo) so a reader can size each photo before the attachments read returns. Empty on a masked row, which is what stops a masked message pulling the blocked member’s uploads.

flag.description: The flag a member added after the message was sent (#3921), or null. Null on a masked row: a tombstone draws no flag.

flagged_by.description: Who added the flag. Null when there is no flag, and also when the viewer blocked the member who added it: the flag stays, the name is withheld.

mentions.description: `users.id` of everyone mentioned, plus a reply's quoted author, resolved server-side at send time. Null on a masked row: a mention overrides a per-channel mute, so leaving it would let a blocked member keep poking the blocker through a masked row.

thread_root_id.description: The parent message when this row is a reply inside a message thread (#3785). Thread replies never appear in the channel timeline; a client that receives one over Realtime must keep it out of the timeline.

thread_reply_count.description: On a thread parent: its reply count, kept by a trigger so the parent’s Realtime UPDATE echo carries it. 0 on every other row.

thread_recent_sender_ids.description: On a thread parent: up to three recent repliers, newest first.

thread_last_reply.description: On a thread parent: its newest reply that isn’t deleted, for the thread card’s preview (#4297). Kept by a trigger, so the parent’s Realtime UPDATE echo carries it. Null on every other row and on a parent whose replies are all deleted. A read that masks withholds it when the viewer blocked that replier (`sender_blocked: true`).

sender_blocked.description: Whether the server masked this row against the caller’s block list. Present on **every** row, not only the masked ones: an absent-means-false flag cannot distinguish “this server does not mask” from “this message is fine”. Not sufficient on its own — rows arriving over the Realtime `postgres_changes` echo carry no viewer, so a client must also apply the list from `GET /v1/chat/blocks`.

width.description: Photo width in pixels, so readers draw the bubble at its shape before the photo loads. A size out of range (1 to 20000), or one without the other, is dropped rather than refused, so a bad size never blocks a send.

thumbhash.description: ThumbHash of the photo, base64: the blurred placeholder readers draw until it loads.

preview_storage_path.description: The `preview_storage_path` the upload-url call returned, once the preview copy is uploaded.

message_ids.description: IDs of already-fetched messages in this channel to resolve avatar paths for. The server derives the avatar path set itself (`chat_messages.author_avatar_path` for rows matching both this channel and this id list) rather than trusting a caller-supplied storage path — the `chat-archive` bucket has no storage RLS, and an avatar path is otherwise indistinguishable from another message's attachment path.

flag.description: One flag per message (#3921). Anyone who can read the channel may flag an unflagged message; replacing a flag takes its sender, whoever added it, or `channels:manage`.

action_type.description: Action discriminator. `reaction:<emoji>` for emoji reactions, `vote` for poll votes (UPSERT), free-form for card actions.

size_bytes.description: File size in bytes, if known. Rejected server-side against the upload size ceiling when present.

with_preview.description: Also mint an upload URL for a smaller JPEG copy of this photo, which readers draw in the timeline. Ignored unless content_type is an image.

for_thread.description: The file is for a reply inside a message thread (#3785). Authorizes as a thread write, which a read-only channel allows, so mint and send agree for a thread reply under an announcement.

upload_url.description: Short-lived signed URL; PUT the bytes to it.

storage_path.description: Storage path to send back as the attachment path when posting the message.

message_id.description: Server-allocated message id embedded in storage_path.

preview_upload_url.description: Only when with_preview was asked for an image: PUT the preview JPEG here, as image/jpeg.

preview_storage_path.description: Only with preview_upload_url: send back as the attachment preview_storage_path.

level.description: all = every message; mentions = only when you are mentioned; off = muted, though @mentions still notify. With no level stored for the channel, a kind-level override applies (outside DMs), else the channel default (officer-set, else `all` for #general, the announcements channel and DMs, `off` for #chapter-audit, `mentions` for the rest); GET /v1/channels/notification-preferences reports it.

sender_id.description: Null for an imported archive message, which names its author in author_name instead.

content.description: Reads “[message deleted]” once the message is deleted — the bookmark keeps its row and surfaces that placeholder rather than disappearing.

sender_blocked.description: Whether the caller has blocked this message’s sender. Present on every row, not only the masked ones. A blocked row’s `content` reads the masking sentinel — never pattern-match it. Distinct from `message_available`, which is about channel access: a block leaves the jump affordance live, and it lands on the same tombstone the timeline shows.

created_at.description: When the caller saved it — not when the message was sent.

message_id.description: The message being reported. Must be one the caller can already read — reporting authorizes as a read of the message’s channel.

details.description: Optional free text from the reporter.

message_id.description: Null once the reported message was hard-deleted (a channel delete, or the Discord import purge). The report outlives it; the reported_* fields are the evidence.

channel_id.description: The channel the message was in when the report was filed. Null once that channel is deleted, and for reports filed before it was recorded whose message was already gone. An id only: it grants no read, and a direct message stays closed to the officer.

reported_content.description: What the member wrote on the message, as it read when the report was filed, so a sender soft-deleting their own message cannot blank the evidence. Usually the message content; for a poll, the content followed by the card question (when it differs) and one `- label` line per option, newline-separated.

reported_sender_id.description: Null for an imported archive message, which names its author in reported_author_name instead.

reported_attachments.description: The message's attachments when the report was filed. Until the report is resolved and its files released, no purge deletes them, so they stay reviewable after the sender deletes the message; once it resolves they are deleted unless another message or report still holds them. Empty for a message with none, and for reports filed before attachments were kept.

status.description: `open` is deliberately not accepted: the answer to “it happened again” is a new report, not a revived one.

download_url.description: Signed download URL, valid for an hour. It forces a download (Content-Disposition: attachment), so opening it saves the file; an still renders an image from it.

message_id.description: Null once the reported message was hard-deleted (a channel delete, or the Discord import purge). The report outlives it; the reported_* fields are the evidence.

channel_id.description: The channel the removed message was in, so a client can blank that one timeline's cached copy instead of refetching every timeline. An id only: it grants no read, and a direct message stays closed to the officer. Null when the message row no longer exists.

reported_content.description: What the member wrote on the message, as it read when the report was filed, so a sender soft-deleting their own message cannot blank the evidence. Usually the message content; for a poll, the content followed by the card question (when it differs) and one `- label` line per option, newline-separated.

reported_sender_id.description: Null for an imported archive message, which names its author in reported_author_name instead.

reported_attachments.description: The message's attachments when the report was filed. Until the report is resolved and its files released, no purge deletes them, so they stay reviewable after the sender deletes the message; once it resolves they are deleted unless another message or report still holds them. Empty for a message with none, and for reports filed before attachments were kept.

message_already_deleted.description: True when the message was already soft-deleted before this call, so nothing was removed now; the report (and any other open report on the message) is marked actioned either way.

blocked_user_ids.description: users.id values the caller has blocked in the active chapter. An empty array means nobody is blocked — a failed request is NOT an empty list, and a client must hold unmaskable messages rather than render them when the read fails.

user_id.description: The `users.id` of the member to block. Must be a member of the active chapter — a block is scoped to one chapter.

unread_only.description: Show only channels with something unread, a mention included. Pinned channels and the open channel still show.

hide_muted.description: Leave out channels whose notification level is off. A muted channel with an unread @-mention still shows.

collapsed_sections.description: Section keys the member folded: pinned, channels, direct, system, or category:<uuid>.

pinned_channel_ids.description: Channels the member pinned to the top, limited to channels they can still read. Carries no order: the sidebar sorts the Pinned section like any other.

unread_count.description: Replies new to the caller; always 0 when muted.

follow_state.description: The caller’s state; null when not following.

state.description: `following` pushes replies within the channel’s level, `muted` never pushes, `none` unfollows.

background.description: What to draw behind the messages column.

source.description: Where it came from: the channel's own setting, the chapter default, or `none` for a DM (always plain).

photo_url.description: A signed URL for the photo when `background` is `photo`; null otherwise, or when signing failed (draw plain).

background.description: A built-in key, `photo` (with `storage_path`), or null to follow the chapter's default.

storage_path.description: Required with `photo`: the path the photo-url call returned.

upload_url.description: Short-lived signed URL; PUT the bytes to it.

storage_path.description: Storage path to send back as `storage_path` when setting the photo.
Required with `photo`: the path the photo-url call returned.

category_id.description: The category the channels are filed under, or null for the default Channels section. A channel listed from another section moves here.

channel_ids.description: Every channel the officer sees in that section, top to bottom. Any other channel already in the section keeps its relative order after them. Never a DM, a group DM or #chapter-audit.

category_ids.description: The chapter’s categories, top to bottom. A category not listed keeps its relative order after them.

sender_id.description: The sender, or null for an imported Discord row.

author_name.description: An imported row's Discord name; null for a member's message.

excerpt.description: The message's first words on one line, at most 140 characters, for the strip's preview.

messages.description: Unseen Important messages flagged in the last 14 days, oldest first, at most 50.

total.description: How many unseen Important messages there are, among at most 1000 flagged in the window.

message_ids.description: Messages the caller jumped to or scrolled onto their screen. Ids the strip does not count are ignored.

point_value.description: Points for attending. On create, kept only when the caller holds `events:update`; anyone else's event is stored with 0, whatever is sent (#3709).

is_mandatory.description: Whether everyone the event invites must attend. On create, kept only when the caller holds `events:update`; anyone else's event is stored as optional, with each role in `required_role_ids` moved to `optional_role_ids` (#3709).

recurrence_rule.description: Repeat rule. Either a legacy token (WEEKLY, BIWEEKLY, MONTHLY: a fixed run of 12, 6 or 6 meetings after the first, still accepted from older phone builds) or an iCalendar RRULE subset such as `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1;BYDAY=MO,TH;COUNT=20;TZID=America/New_York`: FREQ DAILY|WEEKLY|MONTHLY, INTERVAL 1-30, BYDAY (weekly: the days, required; monthly: the nth weekday such as 2TU or -1FR), BYMONTHDAY (monthly by date: 1-31, not with BYDAY), exactly one of COUNT (2-120 meetings, the first included) or UNTIL (YYYYMMDD, inclusive), and TZID (the zone whose wall clock the series keeps).

required_role_ids.description: Roles that must attend. See `others_invited` for members holding none of the listed roles.

excluded_role_ids.description: Roles not invited: their holders do not see the event and cannot check in, unless another role of theirs is listed as required or optional.

others_invited.description: Whether a member holding none of the listed roles is invited (then `is_mandatory` says whether they must attend). Omitted on create, it is stored as null, which reads as true unless `required_role_ids` is non-empty: the older "only these roles" meaning, for a caller that predates this field. Omitted on update, it is left as stored.

check_in_zone.description: Optional check-in geofence: polygon vertices a member must stand inside to check in. At least 3 points; the closing edge is implicit. Omit for an event with no geofence.

check_in_zone_name.description: Human-readable name for `check_in_zone`, shown on the mobile scanner ("Inside the Great Hall zone").

check_in_opens_minutes.description: Minutes before start_time that check-in opens. Omitted on create, it is 10; the window closes 15 minutes after end_time.

event_type_id.description: One of the chapter's event types (`GET /v1/event-types`), or null for none. The type only fills the form: the event's own `point_value` and `is_mandatory` are what count. An id that isn't the chapter's is a 400.

channel_id.description: When set with `client_message_id`, posts an interactive event card to this chat channel after the event is created (the `/event` slash command). Omit for dashboard creates. Rejected with a 400 when the event keeps anyone out (`others_invited` false, including its default when `required_role_ids` is non-empty, or a non-empty `excluded_role_ids`), on this key or `client_message_id` alone — the card is broadcast to every reader of the channel, so a create cannot both limit its audience and post one. (`PATCH` can still limit the audience of an event whose card already posted; that card is left as-is.)

client_message_id.description: Client-generated idempotency key for the chat card, reconciling the optimistic loading placeholder. Required alongside `channel_id`. Rejected with a 400 when the event keeps anyone out, even without `channel_id` — see that field.

others_invited.description: Null on a row written without it: read it as true unless `required_role_ids` is non-empty (`eventOthersInvited` in `@repo/validation`).

check_in_zone.description: Optional check-in geofence. `null` means the event has no zone.

check_in_opens_minutes.description: Minutes before start_time that check-in opens; it closes 15 minutes after end_time.

event_type_id.description: The chapter's event type this was made as, or null. Cleared when the type is deleted.

created_by.description: Who made the event. Null for events made before it was recorded.

card_posted.description: Whether the accompanying chat card was posted. Only an explicit `false` is actionable: the event row committed and the card did not, so no Realtime echo will arrive to reconcile the caller’s optimistic placeholder — drop it and warn, without implying the create failed. Absent means the server reported no outcome (a dashboard create, or a request that did not attempt a card) — leave the placeholder for the echo. Full contract: `spec/behavior/chat/integrations.md` § Slash command dispatch.

recurrence_rule.description: Repeat rule. Either a legacy token (WEEKLY, BIWEEKLY, MONTHLY: a fixed run of 12, 6 or 6 meetings after the first, still accepted from older phone builds) or an iCalendar RRULE subset such as `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1;BYDAY=MO,TH;COUNT=20;TZID=America/New_York`: FREQ DAILY|WEEKLY|MONTHLY, INTERVAL 1-30, BYDAY (weekly: the days, required; monthly: the nth weekday such as 2TU or -1FR), BYMONTHDAY (monthly by date: 1-31, not with BYDAY), exactly one of COUNT (2-120 meetings, the first included) or UNTIL (YYYYMMDD, inclusive), and TZID (the zone whose wall clock the series keeps).

required_role_ids.description: Roles that must attend. See `others_invited` for members holding none of the listed roles.

excluded_role_ids.description: Roles not invited: their holders do not see the event and cannot check in, unless another role of theirs is listed as required or optional.

others_invited.description: Whether a member holding none of the listed roles is invited (then `is_mandatory` says whether they must attend). Omitted, it is left as stored. A stored null reads as true unless `required_role_ids` is non-empty, the older "only these roles" meaning.

check_in_zone.description: Optional check-in geofence: polygon vertices a member must stand inside to check in. At least 3 points; the closing edge is implicit. Omit for an event with no geofence. Send an empty array to clear an existing zone.

check_in_zone_name.description: Human-readable name for `check_in_zone`, shown on the mobile scanner ("Inside the Great Hall zone").

check_in_opens_minutes.description: Minutes before start_time that check-in opens; the window closes 15 minutes after end_time. Omitted leaves it unchanged; null is refused.

event_type_id.description: One of the chapter's event types (`GET /v1/event-types`), or null to clear it; omitted leaves it. The type only fills the form: the event's own `point_value` and `is_mandatory` are what count. An id that isn't the chapter's is a 400.

scope.description: Which occurrences this applies to. `instance` (default) affects only this event. `series` affects the whole recurring series from now forward — occurrences that have already started are never modified or deleted, so attendance history is preserved.

point_value.description: Points for attending, copied onto an event made as this type.

is_mandatory.description: Whether everyone must attend, copied onto an event made as this type.

position.description: The type's place in the chapter's list, lowest first.

name.description: The type as the chapter calls it ("Chapter meeting", "Work party"). Stored trimmed; unique within the chapter, ignoring case.

token.description: Rotating token read from the host QR code (s22). Valid for its 30s window and the one immediately before it.

manualCode.description: Short rotating code typed off the host screen when the camera fails (e.g. "4KQ-88").

lat.description: Scanner latitude. Required when the event defines a check-in geofence; ignored when it doesn't.

lng.description: Scanner longitude. Required when the event defines a check-in geofence; ignored when it doesn't.

attendance.description: The caller's row, or null when they have none (not checked in, and not yet marked).

marked.description: Number of members newly recorded ABSENT. 0 when the event is not mandatory and targets no roles, or when everyone required already has an attendance record.

channel_id.description: When set with `client_message_id`, posts an append-only points card to this chat channel after the ledger write (the `/points` slash command). Omit for dashboard adjustments.

client_message_id.description: Client-generated idempotency key (UUIDv4) for this adjustment. It dedupes the ledger row as well as the chat card: replaying it returns the original transaction rather than granting again, so a request whose response was lost is safe to retry **verbatim** — reusing this id, not a fresh one. Reusing it for a different adjustment, or naming a different `channel_id` than the stored origin, answers 409. Required alongside `channel_id`; the dashboard sends it without one. Full contract: `spec/behavior/points.md` § Anti-Fraud.

metadata.description: Adjustment metadata — `adjusted_by`, `reason`, and `flagged` when the amount met the chapter anomaly threshold.

client_message_id.description: The idempotency key this row was written under, echoed back. `null` for a dashboard adjustment made before the dashboard sent a key; those rows are not deduplicated.

channel_id.description: Origin chat channel this row was written under. A replay re-attempts the points card only into this channel. `null` for dashboard adjustments and for rows committed before the column existed.

card_posted.description: Whether the accompanying chat card was posted. Only an explicit `false` is actionable: the ledger row committed and the card did not, so no Realtime echo will arrive to reconcile the caller’s optimistic placeholder — keep a recorded row and warn, without implying the adjustment failed. Absent means the server reported no outcome (a dashboard adjustment, or a replay of a row with no stored origin channel). A replay whose origin is stored reports this field like a first attempt. Full contract: `spec/behavior/chat/integrations.md` § Slash command dispatch.

success_url.description: URL to redirect on successful payment

cancel_url.description: URL to redirect on canceled payment

return_url.description: URL to redirect when leaving the portal

size_bytes.description: File size in bytes, if known. Rejected server-side against the upload size ceiling when present.

upload_url.description: Short-lived signed URL; PUT the bytes to it.

storage_path.description: Storage path to send on the confirm-upload call.

resource_id.description: Server-allocated resource id embedded in storage_path.

file_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the uploaded file

course_name.description: The course's name ("Calculus I"). Saved only when the course has no name yet; an upload never renames a course.

download_url.description: Short-lived signed URL that downloads the file

files.description: In the order asked. An id not in this chapter, or that could not be signed, is left out.

target_id.description: Id of the row to merge into; the source is deleted

reassigned.description: Count of resources reassigned from source to target

course_number.description: Course number as first saved, e.g. "1010"

course_key.description: The course number trimmed and lowercased; files join a course by department_id and this.

name.description: Omit to keep the stored name. A blank or null clears it (backwork:admin).

add_nicknames.description: Nicknames to add to the list as stored. Open to backwork:upload; a list past the cap is a 400.

remove_nicknames.description: Nicknames to remove from the list as stored, matched case-insensitively. Needs backwork:admin.

points_awarded.description: Whether the approval wrote a SERVICE ledger row. Prefer `awarded_points` for the number.

awarded_points.description: SERVICE points this entry's approval awarded, from the rate read at approval (never recomputed): 0 for a sub-rate duration, null until approved. An entry approved before this field existed whose ledger row is gone also reads null; fall back to `points_awarded` then.

minutes_per_point.description: Minutes of approved service per SERVICE point, as the approve path reads it now (default 60). Approving awards floor(duration_minutes / minutes_per_point).

size_bytes.description: File size in bytes, if known. Rejected server-side against the upload size ceiling when present.

upload_url.description: Short-lived signed URL; PUT the bytes to it.

storage_path.description: Storage path to send as proof_path on the create call.

proof_id.description: Server-allocated proof id embedded in storage_path.

proof_path.description: Storage path to proof file (e.g. from upload)

channel_id.description: When set with `client_message_id`, posts a read-only hours card to this chat channel after the entry is created (the `/hours log` slash command). Omit for dashboard creates. The one-liner cannot attach proof (the Service hours form in the chat composer can) — when `wf_hours_receipt` is on, this route still 400s without `proof_path`.

client_message_id.description: Client-generated idempotency key for the chat card, reconciling the optimistic loading placeholder. Required alongside `channel_id`. Not a server-side dedupe key — a replay creates a duplicate entry.

points_awarded.description: Whether the approval wrote a SERVICE ledger row. Prefer `awarded_points` for the number.

awarded_points.description: SERVICE points this entry's approval awarded, from the rate read at approval (never recomputed): 0 for a sub-rate duration, null until approved. An entry approved before this field existed whose ledger row is gone also reads null; fall back to `points_awarded` then.

card_posted.description: Whether the accompanying chat card was posted. Absent means the server reported no outcome (a dashboard create, or a request that did not attempt a card) — leave the placeholder for the echo. Full contract: `spec/behavior/chat/integrations.md` § Slash command dispatch.

review_comment.description: Optional comment for the member (especially on rejection)

due_at.description: The moment the task is due, when it has a time of day (ISO 8601 with an offset). `due_date` must be the calendar day of this moment as the creator sees it. Omit for a task due on `due_date` with no time.

subtasks.description: Subtasks, in order: a checklist of steps the assignee ticks off (#4003). Blank lines are dropped.

channel_id.description: When set with `client_message_id`, posts an interactive task card to this chat channel after the task is created (the `/task` slash command). Omit for dashboard creates.

client_message_id.description: Client-generated idempotency key for the chat card, reconciling the optimistic loading placeholder. Required alongside `channel_id`.

sent_back_at.description: When an officer last sent the completion back to the assignee; null if never. The assignee taking back their own completion doesn’t set it.

card_posted.description: Whether the accompanying chat card was posted. Only an explicit `false` is actionable: the task row committed and the card did not, so no Realtime echo will arrive to reconcile the caller’s optimistic placeholder — drop it and warn, without implying the create failed. Absent means the server reported no outcome (a dashboard create, or a request that did not attempt a card) — leave the placeholder for the echo. Full contract: `spec/behavior/chat/integrations.md` § Slash command dispatch.

assignee_id.description: User ID of the new assignee. A new assignee starts the task over: it goes back to To do and they are notified.

due_at.description: The moment the task is due, or null to take its time off. Send it with `due_date`: the pair must agree, as on create.

done_at.description: When it was checked off; null while it is still to do.

done.description: True to check it off, false to uncheck it.

position.description: The class's place in the chapter's list, lowest first, which is oldest first.

name.description: The class name as the chapter writes it ("Alpha", "Fall 2019"). Stored trimmed; unique within the chapter, ignoring case.

ids.description: Every one of the chapter's class ids, oldest class first. A list that is not exactly the chapter's current classes is refused with 409, so a stale editor can't drop a class out of order.

pledge_class_id.description: One of the chapter's pledge classes, or null for none.

order_number.description: The member's order within their class, or chapter-wide (a roll or bond number), or null for none. Not required to be unique.

assignments.description: Each listed member gets both values; members not listed are untouched. All of them are written or none.

vote_count.description: Ballot count. Voter names are never returned.

viewer_has_voted.description: Whether the authenticated caller has already voted.

channels.description: Channels being imported: rows with no parent.

discord_channel_name.description: As the scan recorded it; a thread reads `parent › thread`.

parent_discord_channel_id.description: Set on a thread: the channel it lives in.

target_channel_id.description: The Frapp channel it lands in, once known: from mapping time for a merge, and once the worker reaches it for a new channel. Open it at `/chat?channel=<id>`.

counts.description: Channel and thread rows being imported, by status. Rows mapped to skip are in no count.

categories.description: The same rows added up per Discord category, by name (two categories of one name are one line, as they become one group): the channels in no category first, then the categories in Discord's order on a bot import, and on an upload, whose export records no order, in the order the import reaches them. A thread counts under its channel's category. `channels + threads` is the category's total; `done` of that total is finished. Rows mapped to skip are in no count. Empty when the sums could not be read; the rest of the progress still answers.

recent.description: The rows finished last, most recent first, at most 5.

failed.description: Failed rows with the reason, in import order, at most 20. A restart resumes them.

kind.description: `export` is a DiscordChatExporter JSON partition; `media` is a file from its `_Files` folder.

relative_path.description: The path as the export names it, relative to the export folder. This is the join key: the importer resolves an attachment by looking this string up, never by rebuilding a storage key.

part_index.description: Order of this JSON partition. Ignored for media.

upload_url.description: Short-lived signed URL; PUT the bytes to it.

content_type.description: The content type the API validated. Send exactly this on the PUT — the bucket allowlist judges what the uploader sends, and a browser reports an empty type for several formats a Discord archive carries.

mapping_action.description: What to do with this Discord channel. Always explicit — `chat_channels` has no unique constraint on (chapter_id, name), so a same-name match with an existing channel is never treated as an answer. Rows of one import that `create_new` with the same `new_channel_name` (compared trimmed, without a leading `#`, in any case) and the same readers (type, gate and read-only) land in ONE new channel, the one the first of them creates (#2856); rows of the same name with different readers get a channel each.

new_channel_is_read_only.description: Whether the channel `create_new` makes is read-only (only `announcements:post` holders post). Omitted means as in Discord: read-only only when the scan saw Discord make it read-only (`read_only_in_discord`), otherwise postable by whoever can read it. On an uploaded export, which carries no permissions, omitted means postable.

new_channel_visibility.description: Who can read the channel `create_new` makes: the whole chapter, only members holding one of `new_channel_required_permissions` (a ROLE_GATED channel), or `discord` ("Same as Discord"): ROLE_GATED on the read permissions of the Frapp roles mapped (on the roles route) from the Discord roles that could read it. `discord` is for a bot channel the scan saw was private, with at least one of its reader roles mapped; the API works out its permissions and ignores any sent. Omitted or null means not chosen, which is refused unless this is a bot import whose scan saw the channel was public in Discord and holding no private thread. An uploaded export always needs it, and cannot use `discord`.

new_channel_required_permissions.description: Permission strings that can read a `restricted` new channel; a member needs any one. Required and non-empty when `new_channel_visibility` is `restricted`.

new_channel_group.description: The Frapp channel group the channel `create_new` makes goes into, by name: usually its Discord category, when the admin keeps categories as groups. Starting the import puts it in the chapter's group of that name (compared trimmed, in any case), or creates one, after the chapter's own groups and, on a bot import, in Discord's category order. Omitted, null or blank means no group. Ignored unless `mapping_action` is `create_new`: a merge leaves its channel where it is.

action.description: What this Discord role becomes in Frapp: one of the chapter's roles (`frapp_role_id`), a new role created when the import starts (`new_role_name`), or nothing. It decides who reads the channels imported "Same as Discord"; it never assigns anyone to a role.

frapp_role_id.description: Required for `existing`: one of this chapter's roles.

new_role_name.description: Required for `new`: the name to create the role with. It must not match an existing role, ignoring case.

channels.description: Every channel in the server, and the threads of each channel the bot can read, all recorded as `skip` until the admin says otherwise. Threads carry `parent_discord_channel_id` and are not mapped separately — they follow their parent. Each row carries `readable` (whether the bot can read its history; false rows can only be skipped, null means the scan could not tell) and `private_in_discord` (some member could not read its history in Discord; a thread is true when it is a private thread or its channel is private; null means the scan could not tell). A channel that is private, holds a private thread, or whose privacy is null needs an explicit `new_channel_visibility` to be created. A top-level channel also carries `read_only_in_discord`: true when Discord made it read-only, none of its ordinary readers able to talk there (an announcements-style channel; in a forum, able to reply), which is the default for `new_channel_is_read_only`; null when unknown. A top-level channel that was private also carries `discord_reader_role_ids`: the Discord roles (from `roles`) that could read it, each on its own, which is what `new_channel_visibility: discord` copies. Empty when `@everyone` alone could read it (a deny hid it from someone); null when unknown. A top-level channel in a Discord category carries `discord_category` (its name) and `discord_category_position` (its place in the server), which is how the admin keeps categories as channel groups (`new_channel_group`).

roles.description: The roles the chapter can map, highest first as Discord lists them: every role except `@everyone` and the managed roles Discord gives bots and boosters. Empty when they could not be read, which `warnings` says.

warnings.description: What could not be enumerated, in the admin’s words — most often private archived threads, which Discord gates behind a Manage Threads permission this read-only bot deliberately does not request.

messages_after.description: Bot imports only (#2858): import only messages sent at or after this instant. Omit it, or send null, for all history. It is set when the import is first started and fixed from then on: a later start (a restart) may repeat it or leave it out, not change it. An upload's range is set when exporting, with DiscordChatExporter's `--after`, so an upload refuses it.

available.description: False when this environment has no Discord application configured, or when Discord reports that application set up so the connect flow cannot work (checked against Discord, not assumed). The DiscordChatExporter upload flow is unaffected either way — it is a separate path, not a fallback that switches on.

connected.description: Whether this chapter has a Discord server linked.

guild_id.description: The linked Discord server id. Always a string — a snowflake exceeds 2^53 and a JSON round trip through a number would name a different server.

connected_discord_username.description: The Discord account that authorized the install.

return_path.description: Dashboard path to return the browser to once Discord is done, e.g. `/discord-import`. Must be a site-relative path; anything else is replaced with the default. unlinked.description: False when there was no link to remove.

messages_restored.description: How many imported messages went back to their Discord name. Messages the caller deleted stay deleted.
